variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: The GenAI system design process is a repeatable way to turn an uncertain model capability into a bounded product system. It connects a user outcome to an evaluation set, model and context strategy, request budget, safety policy, release gate, and operating feedback loop.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Write the design contract before drawing boxes”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: User outcome
pairs.detail: Name the job, input, expected output, and typed failure response.
pairs.explanation: Name the job, input, expected output, and typed failure response. "Answer an employee's policy question with citations or return insufficient evidence" is testable; "build an AI assistant" is not.

pairs.label: Evidence contract
pairs.detail: State which sources are authoritative, how identity filters them, how fresh they must be, and whether the system may answer without them.
pairs.explanation: State which sources are authoritative, how identity filters them, how fresh they must be, and whether the system may answer without them.

pairs.label: Authority boundary
pairs.detail: Separate model proposals from application authorization.
pairs.explanation: Separate model proposals from application authorization. Name allowed tools, argument validation, approval points, idempotency, and prohibited side effects.

pairs.label: Release evidence
pairs.detail: Define quality slices, safety limits, latency, cost per successful task, availability, and rollback triggers before comparing candidates.
pairs.explanation: Define quality slices, safety limits, latency, cost per successful task, availability, and rollback triggers before comparing candidates.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is every architecture choice must trace to a declared requirement, measurable evidence, and explicit failure behavior.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. User outcome: Name the job, input, expected output, and typed failure response. Evidence contract: State which sources are authoritative, how identity filters them, how fresh they must be, and whether the system may answer without them. Authority boundary: Separate model proposals from application authorization. Release evidence: Define quality slices, safety limits, latency, cost per successful task, availability, and rollback triggers before comparing candidates.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: The GenAI system design process is a repeatable way to turn an uncertain model capability into a bounded product system. It connects a user outcome to an evaluation set, model and context strategy, request budget, safety policy, release gate, and operating feedback loop.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Use the same four-step loop for every candidate”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Frame the decision
pairs.detail: Freeze the outcome, evaluation slice, constraints, and failure cost.
pairs.explanation: Freeze the outcome, evaluation slice, constraints, and failure cost. Do not compare models against different prompts, evidence, or success criteria.

pairs.label: Build a simple baseline
pairs.detail: Start with the shortest viable prompt, no unnecessary tools, and a deterministic application shell.
pairs.explanation: Start with the shortest viable prompt, no unnecessary tools, and a deterministic application shell. The baseline exposes which capability is actually missing.

pairs.label: Add one mechanism
pairs.detail: Try one change at a time: a different tier, retrieval, structured output, a bounded tool, prompt caching, or a human review route.
pairs.explanation: Try one change at a time: a different tier, retrieval, structured output, a bounded tool, prompt caching, or a human review route.

pairs.label: Compare on the same evidence
pairs.detail: Measure task success, critical slices, harmful failures, tokens, latency, and cost.
pairs.explanation: Measure task success, critical slices, harmful failures, tokens, latency, and cost. Keep the mechanism only when the gain justifies its new failure surface.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is every architecture choice must trace to a declared requirement, measurable evidence, and explicit failure behavior.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Frame the decision: Freeze the outcome, evaluation slice, constraints, and failure cost. Build a simple baseline: Start with the shortest viable prompt, no unnecessary tools, and a deterministic application shell. Add one mechanism: Try one change at a time: a different tier, retrieval, structured output, a bounded tool, prompt caching, or a human review route. Compare on the same evidence: Measure task success, critical slices, harmful failures, tokens, latency, and cost.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: The GenAI system design process is a repeatable way to turn an uncertain model capability into a bounded product system. It connects a user outcome to an evaluation set, model and context strategy, request budget, safety policy, release gate, and operating feedback loop.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Release through evidence, rollback, and ownership”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Replay offline
pairs.detail: Compare the candidate with the current baseline on frozen representative cases, critical slices, adversarial inputs, and dependency failures.
pairs.explanation: Compare the candidate with the current baseline on frozen representative cases, critical slices, adversarial inputs, and dependency failures.

pairs.label: Shadow production
pairs.detail: Run the candidate without user-visible effects.
pairs.explanation: Run the candidate without user-visible effects. Compare route decisions, outputs, latency, tokens, and policy verdicts on real traffic.

pairs.label: Canary with limits
pairs.detail: Expose a small eligible cohort, cap spend and side effects, keep a kill switch, and predeclare who may expand or stop the release.
pairs.explanation: Expose a small eligible cohort, cap spend and side effects, keep a kill switch, and predeclare who may expand or stop the release.

pairs.label: Re-evaluate changes
pairs.detail: Treat model, prompt, retrieval, tool, policy, parser, and traffic-distribution changes as versioned releases that can invalidate prior evidence.
pairs.explanation: Treat model, prompt, retrieval, tool, policy, parser, and traffic-distribution changes as versioned releases that can invalidate prior evidence.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is every architecture choice must trace to a declared requirement, measurable evidence, and explicit failure behavior.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Replay offline: Compare the candidate with the current baseline on frozen representative cases, critical slices, adversarial inputs, and dependency failures. Shadow production: Run the candidate without user-visible effects. Canary with limits: Expose a small eligible cohort, cap spend and side effects, keep a kill switch, and predeclare who may expand or stop the release. Re-evaluate changes: Treat model, prompt, retrieval, tool, policy, parser, and traffic-distribution changes as versioned releases that can invalidate prior evidence.
